what_it_does: Large language models (LLMs) store billions of numerical weights; to save memory and speed up computation, researchers 'quantize' those weights — meaning they round the original high-precision decimal numbers to a coarser set of values that fit in fewer bits, somewhat like converting a high-resolution photo to a lower-resolution one. Most approaches pick one number format for an entire layer of the model, but small sub-groups of weights within a single layer can have very different statistical shapes, so a single format fits some groups poorly. M-ANT introduces a flexible number format that can stretch or compress its range to match whichever statistical shape a given sub-group has. A companion hardware unit reads each group's data, selects the best M-ANT variant on the fly, and then fuses the decoding step (converting back to usable numbers) directly into the multiply-accumulate computation so no extra time is lost. A separate fast-path unit handles the model's 'KV cache' — the running scratchpad of keys and values the model builds up as it generates each new word — which must be quantized in real time because it grows dynamically during inference.
